small_guidance:
- Add larger tiles to the autotune list now that the basic config compiles: try `(BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=16/32, num_warps=8, num_stages=2)` and `(BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16, num_warps=8)` — the (OH*OW=15876, OC=128) shape has plenty of M to amortize larger tiles.
- Hoist the per-K index math: precompute `kh`, `kw`, `ic` for the entire K loop once if BLOCK_K covers all of KH*KW (=9) so the inner loop only walks IC; or restructure as nested loops over `ic` (outer) and `kh*kw` (fully unrolled inner) so address arithmetic collapses to constants.
- Swap grid axes so `pid_n` (batch) is the last/least-frequent program_id and `pid_m` is axis 0 — this gives better L2 reuse of the weight tile across spatial tiles within one image; also try a `GROUP_M` swizzle for M/N to improve L2 hit rate on weights.
large_guidance:
- Switch to NHWC (channels_last) layout for both input and output so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous in memory; this removes the strided gather across the channel axis and lets BLOCK_K loads coalesce. Convert input with `x.to(memory_format=torch.channels_last)` and permute weight to `(OC, KH, KW, IC)` once at init.
- Specialize the kernel for `KH=KW=3` as constexprs and fully unroll the 9 spatial taps; make the K loop iterate only over `ic` in chunks of `BLOCK_K_IC`, accumulating 9 small dot products. This eliminates div/mod in the inner loop and exposes more ILP.
- Consider a split-K or persistent-CTA design: with N=128, OH*OW≈15876, OC=128 there is enormous parallelism on (N, spatial) but only 2 tiles along OC at BLOCK_N=64 — a persistent kernel that loops over spatial tiles per SM would amortize weight loads (weights are only 64·128·9·4 ≈ 288 KB and fit easily in L2 across reuse).
